buttonLabel: "How a journey through Argentina, Chile, Ecuador, and Colombia works"
lead: >-
  Buenos Aires and tango, the Atacama Desert, Ecuador's volcanic islands, Cartagena, and Bogotá: four very different stages of a larger South American journey. We explain the actual sequence, flights, climate, and conditions for visiting the Galápagos Islands.
---

## Four countries, four different experiences

[Argentina](/argentina/), [Chile](/chile/), [Ecuador](/ecuador/), and [Colombia](/colombia/) reveal contrasting South American landscapes. In Buenos Aires, the attractions are historic neighborhoods and an evening of tango. Northern Chile brings high-altitude desert, lagoons, and volcanic slopes. Ecuador combines Quito's historic center with the natural world of the Galápagos Islands, while Colombia offers mountain cities, colonial Cartagena, and the Caribbean coast.

The current Ada Tours selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [32-day Eight Countries of South America itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) does visit all four destinations. It also crosses Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Peru, however. **Argentina, Chile, Ecuador, and Colombia do not form a separate, uninterrupted four-country route here.** Bolivia and Peru lie between the Chilean and Ecuadorian sections; altering the itinerary would require recalculating flights and acclimatization.

## The actual order of travel

| Country | What this section includes |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Iguazú, Buenos Aires, city sightseeing, and tango |
| Chile | Santiago, Calama, San Pedro de Atacama |
| Ecuador | Quito, the equator, Santa Cruz, and a sea excursion |
| Colombia | Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena, Bogotá, Zipaquirá |

The [Argentine section](/argentina/) starts at [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) after a visit to the Brazilian side of the waterfalls. A flight then takes the group to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) for a city tour with a Russian-speaking guide and a tango show with dinner. The journey does not stop at Argentina's capital: the next day involves a ferry excursion to Montevideo, so travelers return to Argentina before flying to Chile.

In [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the group explores the historic center and city architecture. A flight to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) follow, preparing travelers for the high-altitude passage through Bolivia. An evening astronomy excursion with a telescope is offered as an optional extra; it must not be assumed to be included. After Atacama come Bolivia's lagoons, the Uyuni Salt Flat, and the Peruvian Andes. Only then does the route reach Ecuador.

The [Ecuadorian section](/ecuador/) begins in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), with sightseeing, historic architecture, the equator, and the Intiñan Museum. After flying to Baltra, travelers meet their guide and cross the Itabaca Channel to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). Visits to the island's highlands and Puerto Ayora are planned. The following day is devoted to a sea excursion: **North Seymour with Bachas Beach, or South Plaza with Cape Carrión**. One of those two alternatives is included; the specific option is confirmed at booking.

From Guayaquil, the program continues to [Colombia](/colombia/). First come [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), Comuna 13, and an excursion to Guatapé and El Peñón Rock. Next is [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) with its historic quarters, followed by [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) with museums, Monserrate, and a day trip to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral. Domestic flights link the major cities. It makes more sense to evaluate the Colombian section by the number of days than by distances on a map.

## Combining cities, desert, islands, and mountains

The current program takes place in late October and November, so different parts of the journey require different clothing. Buenos Aires and Santiago call for comfortable city shoes and an extra layer for evenings. Atacama brings dry air, strong sunshine, and large changes between daytime and nighttime conditions; a warm layer and wind protection are useful for early or late outings. [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) is listed in the program at an altitude of approximately 2,800 m, so avoiding unnecessary exertion in the first hours after arrival is sensible.

On the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), you need sun and wind protection for the sea excursion and footwear appropriate to the confirmed route. Cartagena calls for light clothing again in its warm coastal climate, while Bogotá's elevation and evening conditions differ from those of the Caribbean coast. A single weather forecast for four countries is of little use: prepare by destination and confirm baggage allowances for all domestic flights.

Altitude and personal well-being are another consideration. Between Chile and Ecuador, the complete trip includes a jeep route through Bolivia's highlands, followed by Lake Titicaca and Cusco. Time in San Pedro de Atacama is allocated for acclimatization before Uyuni. **Shortening these sections changes both medical and logistical conditions**: a new itinerary must allow for a sensible rate of ascent. Travelers with cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, or a history of serious altitude-related symptoms, should discuss the route with a doctor before booking.

## Visas, borders, and island documents

Entry requirements depend on nationality and passport type. Travelers from Russia, Europe, and elsewhere may face different visa conditions. We therefore help check **every entry on the actual itinerary**, not just the four countries named by the filter. Consider the Argentine border at Iguazú, re-entry to Argentina after Montevideo, flights through other countries, and the later entry into Colombia.

Chile regulates tourist visits under a temporary-stay regime; whether advance authorization is required depends on nationality and current rules. Passport conditions for Colombia also need to be checked. The Check-Mig electronic form on the migration service's official website is described as a free **optional** pre-registration that may speed up immigration checks; it must not be misrepresented as a universally required paid visa.

The [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) have a **Transit Control Card (TCT)** and separate luggage biosecurity procedures. These apply in addition to ordinary entry into Ecuador. Arrange the confirmed excursion route, transfers to Santa Cruz, and island flight times before departure, as changing the sea-excursion day may affect connections.

## Currencies and spending across countries

Argentina uses Argentine pesos, Chile uses Chilean pesos, Ecuador uses US dollars, and Colombia uses Colombian pesos. The dollar being the currency for one section does not mean it will be convenient to pay cash in every other country. International and Russian-issued card acceptance, fees, bank restrictions, and exchange options must be checked separately. On a group journey, it is useful to allocate a cash reserve in advance for personal purchases, tips, and optional excursions.

The 32-day program described includes 4-star hotels, transfers with drivers, domestic flights, and excursions with Russian- or English-speaking guides depending on the stage. International flights, optional excursions, and personal expenses are excluded. {{#if catalog.hasComparableUsdPrice}}Starting prices for matching programs are from {{catalog.minUsdPriceLabel}}; compare duration, accommodation terms, and the full list of flights when evaluating the price.{{/if}}

An important organizational task is allowing enough time between airports, road transfers, and the ferry excursion. We help coordinate the sequence of countries, hotels, and guides, explain the required documents, and discuss a gentler pace if 32 days of frequent movement feels too demanding. A customized itinerary would be a separate proposal with different service costs.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I combine Argentina, Chile, Ecuador, and Colombia without the other countries?

A tailored itinerary can be discussed. The current [32-day program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also includes Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Peru. Changing the set of countries requires a new calculation of flights and acclimatization time.

### Is the Atacama astronomy excursion included?

The current route includes travel to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), but the telescope astronomy excursion is offered **at additional cost**. Its availability and conditions are confirmed when booked.

### Will we visit both island itineraries in the Galápagos?

No. The sea program provides **one** of two alternatives: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. The choice is confirmed at booking; both together are not included.

### Is Check-Mig required for Colombia?

According to published information from Migración Colombia, it is a free optional pre-registration service. Check current airline and immigration requirements for the particular documents and itinerary before flying.

### Where is altitude most likely to be difficult?

San Pedro de Atacama, Bolivia's subsequent high-altitude section, Titicaca and Cusco, and later Quito and Bogotá all deserve attention. Personal health, the rate of ascent, and an appropriate level of activity are important.

## Four countries for adventure: what is actually included?

[Argentina](/argentina/), [Chile](/chile/), [Colombia](/colombia/), and [Ecuador](/ecuador/) feature in our current themed selection. It contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}, including the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The four countries in the title are **part of an eight-country route**, not a ready-made independent trip limited to exactly those four. Between Chile and Ecuador, the program passes through Bolivia and Peru; Brazil and Uruguay also feature elsewhere in the journey.

Adventure takes different forms along the route: walks around Iguazú, a transition between Atacama and Bolivia's highlands, a sea excursion around the Galápagos, and an eventful day at Guatapé Rock. No confirmed multi-day trek across all four countries, mandatory rafting excursion, or mountaineering ascent appears in the program.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

When choosing, consider **what each day involves**, the number of flights and transfers, rather than simply counting the total days. The physical demands of a waterfall excursion, an island walk, and a climb up stairs differ considerably.

## Argentina: water and Iguazú walking routes

After visiting the Brazilian side of Iguazú Falls, the itinerary continues to the Argentine side near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). A group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide is scheduled. While the Brazilian side provides a broad panoramic view, the Argentine section takes travelers along the park's walkways and closer to the cascades, including [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/) when that area is open.

This part of the journey calls for comfortable shoes, waterproof protection, and careful timing of transfers. Visiting both sides of the falls involves crossing a national border, so documents, park entry rules, and transfer times must be arranged in advance. The itinerary then continues to Buenos Aires, so independently adding a lengthy activity to that day could disrupt connections.

For a more relaxed option, compare [Argentina itineraries](/argentina/tour/) and their actual excursion days, rather than guessing the difficulty level from the word “adventure.”

## Chile: Atacama at the start of a high-altitude crossing

In Chile, travelers explore [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), fly to Calama, and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This stop is used for acclimatization before the high-altitude section. An astronomy excursion is offered as an option, but it depends on confirmation and observing conditions.

Next comes a two-day 4×4 jeep journey to Bolivia's lagoons and salt flats, including [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). **This is an adventure section of the full tour, but it lies outside the four countries in this filter.** The Bolivian jeep tour must not be described as an excursion within Chilean Atacama or promised on a separate four-country itinerary without designing a new program.

The practical concern here is not sporting fitness for trekking but changes in altitude, cold nights, long vehicle journeys, and limited comfort on the highland section. Travelers with chronic illnesses or sensitivity to altitude should discuss the route with a doctor beforehand.

## Ecuador: the Galápagos, lava tunnels, and one of two island routes

After Peru, the itinerary travels through Quito to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). On [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), an excursion to the [island's highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) includes observing giant tortoises and exploring lava tunnels.

The following excursion day involves **a choice between two routes**, not a visit to every listed site: either [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach, or [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Cape Carrión. The specific route is confirmed after booking. The sea excursion is included, but both alternatives cannot be promised together.

The difference matters in practice. Boarding arrangements, time at sea, susceptibility to motion sickness, disembarkation, and the walking portion depend on the chosen route. On protected islands, visitors must follow rules around wildlife and the instructions of their guides.

## Colombia: Guatapé, city walks, and a possible rock ascent

The Colombian section begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). A separate excursion visits [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/). Climbing the stairs up the rock is a possible activity in the area, but the actual opportunity and conditions should be checked against that day's itinerary. Travelers who prefer not to climb can appreciate the scenery, waterfront, and brightly painted buildings of Guatapé.

The route then covers [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/) in Medellín, [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), and [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). These are mainly active city excursions linked by transfers, not a continuous sports journey. Kayaking, canyoning, or rafting cannot simply be added to the included services because such activities are available in Colombia.

## Planning activity levels, flights, and equipment

| Section | Main consideration |
|---|---|
| Iguazú | Wet paths and a border |
| Atacama–Bolivia | Altitude, cold, jeeps |
| Galápagos | Sea travel and regulated visits |
| Guatapé | Walking and a possible ascent |

Bring shoes with good grip, rain protection, warm layers for high elevations, and sun protection. For the day at sea, consider your personal tolerance for motion sickness in advance. Domestic airlines' baggage restrictions should be checked separately; the allowance on an international flight does not determine the rules for the remaining sectors.

We help coordinate excursion days, connections, and reasonable buffer time. If you want a trip limited to Argentina, Chile, Ecuador, and Colombia, a new sequence of flights must be planned and a decision made about the Bolivian jeep section and Peruvian stops. The [general catalog for this country combination](/multi-country/argentina_chile_colombia_ecuador/) provides the geographic overview, while [multi-country adventure itineraries](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) offer other regional options.

## Frequently asked questions about the active itinerary

### Is trekking included in every one of the four countries?

No. The confirmed program includes sightseeing walks, island visits, and extensive transfers. No specialist multi-day trek across all four countries is listed.

### Can we visit North Seymour and South Plaza in one day?

This tour offers one of the two island alternatives. The final choice is agreed after booking; both routes are not included together.

### Where does the jeep route to Uyuni take place?

It begins after Chile's San Pedro de Atacama and continues through Bolivia. It is part of the complete [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), not a separate adventure within the four countries in the title.

  Buenos Aires and tango, Santiago's historic center, Medellín's neighborhoods, colonial Cartagena, Bogotá's museums, and the equator in Ecuador. Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador form part of a large journey in which the cultural program also visits other South American countries.

## Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador: a journey through urban history

Travelers encounter different cultural traditions in [Argentina](/argentina/), [Chile](/chile/), [Colombia](/colombia/), and [Ecuador](/ecuador/). Buenos Aires is associated with tango and urban history; Santiago with civic squares and government buildings; Colombia with transformed neighborhoods, museums, and colonial cities; and Ecuador with Quito's heritage and sites around the equator.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}, featuring a [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The key point about this filter is that the four countries in the title **do not cover the whole itinerary**. The complete journey begins in Brazil and passes through Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, and Ecuador before reaching Colombia. Inca monuments in Peru and Tiwanaku in Bolivia are part of the tour but belong geographically to other countries.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

Within the four selected countries, the focus is city-based cultural excursions. When choosing a journey, look not only at museums but also at the sequence of flights, transfer times, and which visits are actually scheduled.

## Argentina: Buenos Aires, its neighborhoods, and an evening of tango

The Argentine section begins with Iguazú Falls, after which travelers fly to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). A city tour with a Russian-speaking guide introduces neighborhoods including [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/), [San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/), Recoleta, and other parts of the capital.

The cultural evening continues with a [tango show including dinner and transfers](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-dinner-transfer/). Tango is best understood as part of the Buenos Aires city experience: discovering its neighborhoods by day gives context to the evening performance. The relationship between music, dance, and everyday urban life is central here.

The complete itinerary also features a ferry trip to Montevideo after Buenos Aires. But [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is in Uruguay, which does not appear in this four-country selection's title. That day must be counted in the overall duration rather than presented as an excursion within Argentina.

## Chile: Santiago's historic center before the journey to Atacama

In [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a [tour of the historic center and modern districts](/chile/santiago-de-chile/santiago-historic-east-russian-group/) is scheduled. Its urban section covers the Plaza de Armas area, the surroundings of La Moneda Palace, and other landmarks of the capital. The itinerary demonstrates how the historic heart of the city coexists with modern business and residential districts.

A visit to wineries in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) is also offered from Santiago, but it has its own theme and additional cost. Winery visits should not be treated as a mandatory historical and cultural activity in this selection.

The journey then goes via Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and onward toward Bolivia. The historical city visit in Chile is therefore relatively short. If an additional museum or architecture tour is a priority, it should be discussed before flights are confirmed.

## Colombia: urban history from Medellín to Bogotá

The Colombian section offers the most varied range of urban cultural experiences. In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), there is a [tour including Comuna 13](/colombia/medellin/medellin-city-and-comuna-13/). Travelers learn about changes to the urban environment and see its street art. [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/) is a real residential district, so its story should be linked to residents' lives, not reduced to photographs of graffiti.

The itinerary continues to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) for sightseeing in the historic part of the city. The heritage here is different: Caribbean fortifications, colonial architecture, squares, and narrow streets. Cartagena differs from Medellín in climate as well as historical development, making the visits complementary.

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), a [city tour covering the historic center, Gold Museum, and Monserrate](/colombia/bogota/bogota-city-tour/) is planned. A separate day is devoted to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its [Salt Cathedral](/colombia/zipaquira/zipaquira-salt-cathedral-5-hours/). Check actual museum opening days: the tour's terms note restrictions for the Gold Museum, Casa de Moneda, and the Botero Collection. If the dates change, sightseeing must be coordinated with each site's schedule.

| City | Main cultural theme |
|---|---|
| Medellín | Urban history and Comuna 13 |
| Cartagena | Historic Caribbean city |
| Bogotá | Museums, old center, and Monserrate |
| Zipaquirá | Underground Salt Cathedral |

This sequence shows that Colombia is more than a single sightseeing tour of its capital.

## Ecuador: Quito, the equator, and the distinction between culture and nature

After Peru, travelers arrive in Quito. The next day includes city sightseeing and visits to [Mitad del Mundo](/ecuador/place/mitad-del-mundo/) and the Intiñan Museum. Here the introduction to Ecuador's history and geography is connected to the equator.

The journey then heads to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The island section is primarily about nature: the Santa Cruz highlands, giant tortoises, and one of two alternative sea-excursion routes. These activities belong to the **complete cultural and nature journey**, but it would be inaccurate to describe them as excursions to Quito's historic monuments.

For travelers, this means a change of format: first a city day with road transfers, then air and sea travel with their own visiting regulations. Those wishing to spend more time in Quito's museums or historic architecture would need to adjust the schedule before the island flight.

## How the other countries relate to the complete journey

When comparing the four selected countries with the [complete 32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), pay attention to Peru and Bolivia. In Bolivia, the route visits Tiwanaku; in Peru, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). These sites are important to the historical theme of the larger journey but are not in Argentina, Chile, Colombia, or Ecuador.

The tour includes several types of guided excursions and many domestic flights. Decide on priorities before booking: which city visits are essential, where an additional museum is worthwhile, and where an introductory tour is sufficient. A route through exactly the four named countries would require a separate flight plan because the ready-made itinerary connects them via other countries.

We help coordinate time at each stop, excursions, and the sequence of cities. Compare available options in the [general catalog for these four countries](/multi-country/argentina_chile_colombia_ecuador/) and [multi-country culture and history trips](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about the cultural journey

### Can I visit all four countries without Bolivia and Peru?

A tailored itinerary can be discussed. The published 32-day tour travels through eight countries, so excluding Bolivia and Peru would change flights, the number of days, and the excursions.

### Are Bogotá's museums included in the itinerary?

The Bogotá city tour follows the scheduled route, but some museums have closing days. Check the individual stops against the excursion date and actual operating schedules.

### Is visiting the Galápagos part of the historical theme?

The Galápagos section is predominantly a nature and expedition experience. The historical and cultural visits in Ecuador on this itinerary are primarily associated with Quito and the equator.

lead: >-
  One journey can reveal Iguazú's humid forests and waterfalls, the dry foothills of Atacama, the island scenery of the Galápagos, and Guatapé Rock above its reservoir. Here we explain where the route actually goes, which nature excursions are included, and how the four countries differ.

## From waterfalls to islands: four countries' natural landscapes on one journey

[Argentina](/argentina/), [Chile](/chile/), [Colombia](/colombia/), and [Ecuador](/ecuador/) offer different natural attractions. In our selection, they form part of the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The four names in the title therefore represent a themed intersection rather than a ready-made itinerary limited to these countries.

The current catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Beyond the four named countries, the wider program visits Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Peru. Its nature experiences consist of specific stops: the Argentine side of Iguazú, the San Pedro de Atacama area, the Galápagos Islands, and an excursion to El Peñón de Guatapé. Traveling between these places takes additional days.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Argentina: Iguazú, water, and subtropical forest

Argentina's principal nature highlight is near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). The itinerary includes a group excursion on the Argentine side of the waterfalls with a Russian-speaking guide. Travelers first see the Brazilian side: the same river gorge offers different perspectives from the two banks and their viewpoints.

The Argentine walking routes pass along boardwalks among humid vegetation, over waterways, and close to the cascades. One of the best-known features is [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/). Access to a specific path depends on water levels and decisions by the park administration: an attraction appearing in the itinerary does not guarantee that its particular viewing balcony will be accessible on the day of the visit.

After the excursion, a flight to Buenos Aires is scheduled. Do not expect to add a lengthy independent forest walk on the same day: the nature visit is already tied to a transfer and an air connection. The key experience is the power of the water and the forested valley, not a separate multi-day trek.

## Chile: the Atacama Desert and the road toward high altitude

The Chilean section begins in Santiago and continues with a flight to Calama. A transfer then takes travelers to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), a starting point for the desert landscapes of northern Chile. Dry air, wide open spaces, volcanic silhouettes, and marked temperature changes between day and night replace Iguazú's humid forest environment.

This stop has an important limitation in the program. **The main purpose of the day in San Pedro is acclimatization before traveling into Bolivia.** An evening astronomy excursion is offered separately; the basic itinerary does not include visits to every famous valley, salt flat, or geyser in Atacama.

The next nature section does indeed pass high-altitude lagoons, geothermal areas, and salt flats, but **on Bolivian territory**. Confusing it with a Chilean excursion would distort both the geography of the trip and the time allowed for the border crossing. Details of the larger passage are included in the [tour itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

## Ecuador: from high-altitude Quito to the Galápagos Islands

After Peru, the journey continues to [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). The included excursion focuses on the city and the equator. Although Ecuador is known for volcanic landscapes, this tour does not include an independent Cotopaxi ascent or a separate trek on the volcano.

The main nature immersion begins on the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). After flying to Baltra, travelers cross the Itabaca Channel to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). Driving across the island reveals changes in vegetation from dry shores to wetter inland areas. In the [Santa Cruz highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/), you visit giant tortoise habitat.

The following day is an included sea excursion with **one of two alternatives**, not a tour of all four locations: North Seymour and Bachas Beach, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. The particular option is confirmed after booking. Weather, sea conditions, and protected-area rules affect landings, and an encounter with a particular animal cannot be guaranteed by the wildlife theme alone.

## Colombia: Guatapé Rock and the patchwork of the reservoir

In Colombia, the most striking natural landmark on this itinerary is [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/). An excursion from Medellín combines the rock formation with [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/): a stony summit, water, and green banks create scenery quite unlike Iguazú or the dry Altiplano.

The surrounding reservoir is man-made, which is important to understanding the place: its islands and winding bays emerged when the valley was transformed. Climbing the stairs up the rock requires consideration of personal fitness and access conditions; a stop near the rock does not mean that every traveler must ascend to the summit.

Other days in Colombia are mainly city-focused: Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá, and Zipaquirá. An expedition into Colombia's jungles or dedicated wildlife observation would require a different itinerary.

## Comparing the natural experiences

| Section | Main natural highlight |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Waterfalls and humid forest |
| Chile | Desert and volcanic views |
| Ecuador | Islands, shores, and highlands |
| Colombia | Rock formation and reservoir |

These stops also differ in how they are visited. At Iguazú, waterproof protection and suitable shoes for walkways are useful; in Atacama, prepare for temperature changes; in the Galápagos, plan for travel at sea. The full 32-day itinerary passes through high-altitude Bolivia and Peru between Chile and Ecuador, so overall exertion is determined by the entire route.

For a journey primarily about geology, waterfalls, and panoramic views, explore the [Nature interest](/interests/nature/). If giant tortoises, birds, and other animals are your main motivation, compare the [Wildlife and Safari selection](/interests/wildlife/). The [general catalog for this combination](/multi-country/argentina_chile_colombia_ecuador/) also shows routes without a nature filter.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in these four countries

### Is there a ready-made trip exclusively through Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador?

This selection includes a tour covering eight countries. If you want only the four named countries, the itinerary, duration, flights, and price would need to be agreed as a different program.

### Is an excursion to all the famous Atacama nature sites included?

No. On the current program, San Pedro de Atacama serves primarily as an acclimatization stop, and the evening astronomy excursion is offered separately. The main two-day jeep section takes place in Bolivia.

### Can both Galápagos sea routes be visited?

The current itinerary includes one of two alternatives. North Seymour with Bachas and South Plaza with Cape Carrión do not automatically form two included excursions.

### When should I check the availability of Iguazú's walkways?

Before the trip and again shortly before visiting. Individual paths and viewpoints may temporarily close because of water levels or infrastructure conditions even when the park as a whole remains open.

## Nature across Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Ecuador on one journey

[Argentina](/argentina/), [Chile](/chile/), [Colombia](/colombia/), and [Ecuador](/ecuador/) offer waterfalls, desert scenery, mountain valleys, and island nature. But a Wildlife and Safari filter does not mean that every day or every country is devoted to wild animals.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It features a [32-day eight-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) that connects these four countries with Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, and Peru. Nature experiences are distributed unevenly: **the principal excursions for observing island wildlife take place in the Galápagos**, waterfalls are visited at the Argentina–Brazil border, and scenery and urban sightseeing dominate the Chilean and Colombian sections.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

This suits travelers who want the continent's natural diversity alongside its cities and monuments. The program does not include a dedicated safari through all four countries, separate multi-day birdwatching expeditions, or guaranteed encounters with rare animals.

## Argentina: Iguazú and humid tropical forest

Argentina's main nature stop is near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and the waterfalls. Travelers first see the Brazilian side, followed by the Argentine side on the next excursion day. One of the most famous areas is [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/). Access to particular walkways and viewpoints should be checked against park conditions for the visit date.

Humid forest and many bird species occur around the waterfalls, but sightings of particular animals are not guaranteed. The central included activity on the Argentine day is the waterfall excursion. Optional activities such as the Bird Park may be offered in Brazil, but they **do not automatically become included visits** under this four-country filter.

A valuable feature of the itinerary is the chance to compare the same natural complex from both sides of an international border. Panoramas from Brazil and walkways in Argentina offer different views, while transfer time depends on document controls, excursion tickets, and transport schedules. A flight to Buenos Aires follows the Argentine visit, so adding a long independent walk without prior coordination is unwise.

## Chile: Atacama's stark scenery and the transition to high altitude

In Chile, travelers spend time in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), then arrive via Calama in [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). A stop is planned here to adapt to high altitude. An optional evening astronomy excursion requires separate confirmation.

Atacama is famous for its dry desert landscapes, but the itinerary **does not include a separate mandatory wildlife-watching day in Chile**. The following major nature section, with high-altitude lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat, takes place **in Bolivia**: a two-day jeep journey begins after crossing the border and continues across Bolivian territory.

This distinction matters for an accurate description. Photographs of Bolivia's lagoons, geysers, and salt flats cannot automatically be assigned to Chile simply because the trip begins in Atacama.

## Ecuador: giant tortoises and Santa Cruz lava tunnels

Ecuador is the key section for Wildlife and Safari. Travelers fly from Quito to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), arrive via Baltra, and continue to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The arrival day includes an [excursion through the Santa Cruz highlands to see giant tortoises and lava tunnels](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-lava-tunnels/).

In the [Santa Cruz highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/), travelers explore the island's terrestrial ecosystems and giant tortoise habitat. The excursion takes place in natural areas; the animals' behavior depends on natural conditions, and visitors must follow restrictions protecting the site. Tortoises must not be touched, fed, or disturbed for photographs.

The following day is a sea excursion. The itinerary includes **exactly one of two options**:

- [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach.
- [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Cape Carrión.

The full description contains both routes as alternatives, but **visiting both is not promised**. The specific option is confirmed after booking. The islands provide opportunities to observe natural habitats and wildlife, but neither a list of animals sighted nor favorable sea conditions can be guaranteed in advance.

## Colombia: Guatapé and the landscapes around Medellín

In Colombia, the nature experiences are part of a route otherwise dominated by cities. A journey from [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) visits [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/). Famous views of water and green hills make this day particularly attractive for landscape photography.

The Guatapé trip, however, is a scenic excursion, **not a safari** or a specialist wildlife-watching outing. The route then continues to Cartagena, Bogotá, and Zipaquirá, where historical, urban, and cultural sites dominate. The program does not include separate visits to Colombian national parks specifically to observe fauna.

If wildlife and protected natural areas are your main priority, compare [wildlife-watching tours](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) and the number of planned naturalist excursions. If waterfalls, deserts, and mountain views matter more, explore [nature itineraries](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

## Preparing for very different natural environments

| Route section | What to consider |
|---|---|
| Iguazú | Moisture, tropical forest, walkways |
| Chile and Bolivia | Altitude, sunshine, cold nights |
| Galápagos | Sea crossings, national park rules |
| Guatapé | Walks and scenic viewpoints |

A rain jacket and shoes with good grip help at Iguazú. Warm layers and strong sun protection are important in the highlands. For the Galápagos, plan for time on a boat and suitable footwear for authorized walks. Check baggage allowances separately for domestic flights.

Altitude tolerance also deserves attention. Temperatures and elevation change considerably between the lowland tropics, Atacama, Bolivia, and Peru. Travelers with personal medical risks should consult a doctor before booking.

Start with the experience you most want. If giant tortoises and island wildlife are the main goal, the Ecuadorian section on Santa Cruz and the sea excursion day are the most substantial in this selection. If waterfalls and forest are the priority, focus on Iguazú. Guatapé's scenery and cities dominate Colombia, while Chile introduces the desert environment.

## Frequently asked questions about nature and wildlife

### Can we see giant tortoises in the Galápagos?

The itinerary includes an excursion to the Santa Cruz highlands, where giant tortoises are a principal focus. They remain wild animals, so actual sightings and the distance to them depend on visiting conditions.

### Do we visit both North Seymour and South Plaza?

No. The day at sea involves choosing one of two alternatives: North Seymour with Bachas, or South Plaza with Cape Carrión. The option is confirmed after booking.

### Is a separate Colombian safari included?

No. The Colombian portion includes a visit to Guatapé and city excursions, while the main wildlife-watching experience is in Ecuador.
